concept.movement: Quiet buoyant swimming, driven by a coherent dorsoventral tail stroke, with restrained body pitch and relaxed steering flippers; faster travel increases the tail beat rather than adding a ground gait.
concept.attack: A defensive forward shoulder and muzzle shove, with the flippers bracing laterally and the tail providing the impulse, followed by a smooth recoil.
concept.death: The tail beat fades, the body settles forward onto separate belly patches, the chin lowers, and both flippers relax onto the bottom before a still hold.

concept.death: Propulsion fades, the body glides forward and sinks onto separate belly supports. The rostrum lowers, the flippers relax and the flukes settle without rolling the animal onto its side.

concept.death: The traveling wave fades into a relaxed shallow S. The front body and skull lower, the belly settles in several disjoint regions, and the entire body holds still without rolling.

concept.death: Tail propulsion fades and the fish drifts down into a supported forward rest on separate head and belly regions. Fins fold or relax clear of the bottom rather than holding the body up on a single fin tip; the natural upward tail silhouette is retained when clearance allows.
